content: The laboratory within the premises conducted an LF-LAM test immediately, which yielded a positive result. A sample was subsequently sent to the laboratory for MC-aNAAT testing, which confirmed the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). The test results indicated susceptibility to rifampicin (RIF) but resistance to isoniazid (INH). The detected INH resistance necessitated further investigation as per algorithm 4. A genotypic drug susceptibility test (DST) using a second-line line-probe assay (LPA), available in the laboratory, was performed, and fluoroquinolone (FQ) resistance was detected. Consequently, the treatment regimen was adjusted to an individualized plan. An additional sample was collected and sent to the national reference laboratory for phenotypic DST. In a high TB/HIV setting, a presumptive TB patient underwent Xpert MTB/RIF testing, which detected RIF-susceptible TB. First-line TB treatment was initiated. However, due to the high prevalence of isoniazid-resistant TB (Hr-TB) in the setting, testing for INH resistance was required. A second sample was collected and tested using LC-aNAAT, which confirmed INH resistance. The results also indicated susceptibility to fluoroquinolones. The treatment was modified to an Hr-TB regimen with the addition of levofloxacin. In a high RIF-resistance prevalence setting, a patient was diagnosed with multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) using MC-aNAAT. SL-LPA testing was performed, and pyrazinamide (PZA) resistance was detected using HC-rNAAT. Phenotypic DST was also conducted, and the treatment was adjusted based on the resistance pattern. The patient was referred to a specialized center for individualized treatment, and an additional sample was collected for further genoand phenotypic DST. The examples illustrate the importance of diagnostic tools like MC-aNAAT, which can simultaneously detect INH and RIF resistance at the initial TB diagnosis. They also highlight the need to consider local epidemiological contexts, such as high Hr-TB or RIF-resistance prevalence, to guide testing and treatment decisions. Centralized models with sample referral networks are essential for addressing patient needs, particularly in settings with limited laboratory capacity.
